Dad's Famous Sourdough Loaf
Recipe Checks & Photos Schedule TroubleshootingFixes
Recipe

74.5% hydration, long cold proof for blisters, tight shape for height. KitchenAid 6qt with the dough hook, never above speed 2.

Ingredients

4 loaves won't fit in one 6qt bowl. Mix two batches of 2 loaves about 15 minutes apart. Amounts below are the total for all 4; the method shows per-batch amounts.

Whole wheat is optional. To skip it, use all bread flour (500g per loaf) and hold back an extra 5–10g water at first. Expect a milder flavor, a slightly slower bulk, and possibly a touch more height.

Why it works

Height

Bread flour plus mixer kneading builds a strong gluten network that holds gas. Stopping bulk at 50–75% rise leaves fuel for oven spring. The lid traps steam so the crust stays soft long enough to expand.

Blisters

The long cold proof builds acids and gas under a moist surface. Cold dough hitting a 475°F pot puffs those pockets and browns them.

Before every bake

Starter doubles within 4–6 hrs of feeding
Oven thermometer checked
Container has a tape mark at the starting level
Probe thermometer ready for dough and loaf temps
Checks & Photos

Go by these signs, not the clock.

Readiness checks

Before step 2 · Starter

Use it at its peak

Ready: doubled or more since feeding (rubber band on the jar), domed top just starting to flatten, bubbly throughout, smells tangy and yeasty.
Not yet: not doubled, so wait. Too late: collapsed with streaks down the jar, or smells like nail polish. Feed again and wait for the next peak.

Float test (optional): a spoonful that floats is ready. Whole wheat starters can sink even when ready, so trust the doubling first.

End of step 3 · Windowpane test

Gluten developed enough

Ready: a golf-ball piece stretches slowly into a thin, translucent sheet before tearing.
Tears fast: mix 1–2 more minutes on speed 2. A partial windowpane is fine at this hydration; the folds finish the job.
End of step 4 · Bulk ferment

Stop at 50–75%, not doubled

Ready: 50–75% rise on the tape mark, domed edges, bubbles on top and sides, jiggles when you shake the container.
Not yet: check every 30 min. Doubled or sloppy: shape now and expect less height.
After cold proof · Poke test

Proofed and ready to bake

Ready: a floured finger poked 1/2 inch springs back slowly and leaves a small dent.
Springs back fast: more fridge time, or 30–60 min at room temp. No spring back: bake now and score shallow.
End of step 10 · Done baking

Fully baked

Ready: 208°F internal, deep mahogany crust, hollow thump on the bottom.
Not yet: 5 more minutes uncovered, then check again.
